name: Basic Health & Safety
description: An entry-level introduction to health and safety at work. The course covers the basics of the Occupational Health and Safety Act, common workplace hazards, safe work practices, personal protective equipment, housekeeping and emergency procedures. Learners come away knowing how to spot unsafe conditions, protect themselves and others, and report hazards or incidents correctly. It suits new employees, general workers and anyone who needs a practical grounding in workplace safety. On completion, learners receive a certificate in line with SAQA-aligned training.
outcomes: Explain the basic purpose of the Occupational Health and Safety Act and the duties of employers and employees
Identify common workplace hazards and unsafe conditions
Apply safe work practices and use personal protective equipment correctly
Respond to emergencies and report hazards or incidents
Maintain good housekeeping in the work area
audience: Anyone who needs a practical grounding in workplace safety
Small business owners and their staff

faqs.a: The course costs R700 per learner and runs for one day. Group bookings are negotiable. We train online, on site at your premises, or at our centres in Midrand and Durban, with daily classes and no waiting period. WhatsApp 061 580 7967 to book or request a group quote. You can also call 010 746 6954.

faqs.q: What unit standard is this aligned to?
faqs.a: The course is aligned to unit standard 242974, Apply flagging procedures to control traffic, at NQF level 2. It covers traffic control plans, correct hand signals, flagging equipment and PPE, managing vehicles and pedestrians, and personal safety on the road. Learners receive a certificate in line with SAQA-aligned unit standards.

faqs.q: Who should attend flagman training?
faqs.a: Anyone assigned to stop-and-go traffic control: flagmen, traffic controllers and road construction or maintenance workers. The work is dangerous, so proper training in hand signals, positioning and awareness is essential. The course also covers emergency situations and how to respond. It is also useful for site supervisors who manage traffic control teams. One day, with daily classes.

faqs.q: Do I need experience before I can do this course?
faqs.a: No previous traffic control experience is required. The course starts with the role of the flagman and the hazards of traffic control areas, then teaches the correct procedures and hand signals. Delegates practise the signals and controls during the day and receive a certificate on completion. Classes run daily and group rates are negotiable.

faqs.q: What qualification does this programme lead to?

faqs.q: Who should attend this programme?
faqs.a: The programme suits aspiring safety officers, SHE representatives, safety assistants and anyone building a career in occupational health and safety. faqs.q: Do I need experience before I can do this programme?

The programme starts with the fundamentals, including applying health and safety to a work area, then builds to legislation, investigations and inspections. name: Traffic Safety Officer
audience: Traffic safety officers and traffic controllers

faqs.q: How much does the Traffic Safety Officer course cost?
faqs.a: The course costs R2,800 per learner and runs over three days. Group bookings are negotiable. Training is available online, on site at your premises, or at our centres in Midrand and Durban, with daily classes and no waiting period. WhatsApp 061 580 7967 to book or ask about group rates.

faqs.q: What does the course cover?
faqs.a: The course covers legislative requirements, health and safety in roadwork areas, hazard identification, reading traffic accommodation and construction drawings, erecting temporary traffic control equipment, and implementing roadside safety measures. It includes unit standards 14558, 9964, 14580 and 14561. The training is practical, with hands-on work over the three days. Delegates receive a certificate in line with SAQA-aligned unit standards.

faqs.q: Do I need experience before I can do this course?
faqs.a: You need basic literacy and numeracy, and you must be medically fit to work in roadside and construction environments. No previous traffic control experience is required. The three-day course teaches the practical skills for the job, from reading drawings to erecting traffic control equipment and managing roadside safety. It is also the entry route for people starting in traffic control.

faqs.q: Can you train at our site?
faqs.a: Yes. On-site training at your premises is available anywhere in South Africa, which suits road construction and maintenance teams. Online and centre-based options are also offered at our Midrand and Durban centres. Group pricing is negotiable. Daily classes mean you can book without a waiting period.
